from manim import *
import os

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear systems are intersections of geometric objects.",
            "Equations define lines or planes in space.",
            "The solution is where these objects meet.",
            "Robots A and B track these specific paths.",
            "Their collision point is the unique solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems", lecture_lines)
        
        # Paths for robots
        line1 = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=WHITE)
        line2 = Line(start=self.grid["E1"], end=self.grid["B6"], color=WHITE)
        intersecting_lines = VGroup(line1, line2)
        self.place_in_area(intersecting_lines, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight intersection point as solution
        collision_dot = Dot(self.grid["C4"], color=YELLOW, radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(collision_dot, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        label = Text('Solution', font_size=24).next_to(collision_dot, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(collision_dot), Write(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Robots A and B
        robotA = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg").set_color(GREEN)
        robotB = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg").set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(robotA, 'B1', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(robotB, 'E1', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(robotA), FadeIn(robotB))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Collision
        self.play(
            robotA.animate.move_to(collision_dot.get_center()),
            robotB.animate.move_to(collision_dot.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(Flash(collision_dot, color=RED, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce linear systems as the intersection of geometric objects (lines/planes). Explain that a solution exists only where these objects meet. Visualize a 2D system as two lines intersecting at a point.
sections.example: Imagine two smart-robots (A and B) moving along paths defined by equations. Their collision point is the unique solution to the system.

sections.title: The Role of Inverse Matrices
sections.content: Explain that an invertible matrix represents a transformation that doesn't collapse dimensions. If a matrix is invertible, the 'robot's' path can be perfectly reversed. Connect this to the determinant: non-zero determinant = space is preserved.
sections.example: Think of an invertible matrix as a 'transformation gate' that stretches a square grid. The inverse matrix is the 'undo button' that snaps the grid back to its original shape.

sections.title: Column Space: The Reachable World
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the column vectors. It is the set of all possible 'destinations' the transformation can reach. Use a 3D animation showing vectors generating a plane or a line.
sections.example: A 3D printer head has three motors. The column space represents every point in the XYZ coordinate system that the printer head can physically reach.

sections.title: Null Space: The Hidden Dimensions
sections.content: Explain Null Space as the set of vectors that are 'squashed' to the origin by the transformation. This is the 'hidden' part of the system that disappears during the process.
sections.example: If a camera lens flattens a 3D scene into a 2D photo, the 'depth' axis that vanishes into the photo's plane represents the null space of the projection matrix.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Link the concepts: A system has a solution if the target vector lies within the Column Space. If the Null Space is non-trivial, the solution is not unique (multiple paths lead to the same destination).
sections.example: Review: Inverting a map (Inverse), finding the reachable zone (Column Space), and identifying obscured details (Null Space) are the three pillars of solving complex linear systems.
